findings.flaw_category: Local individuals minted in third-party namespaces
findings.evidence: FASTO_RDF(6).owl declares FASTO as the ontology at lines 33-40, but declares local domain individuals in non-FASTO namespaces: temporal.owl#hours and temporal.owl#lantus are owl:NamedIndividual at lines 127182-127185 and 127214-127218; temporal.owl#minutes is an owl:NamedIndividual at lines 127249-127252; ssn/patient_1_BAN is an owl:NamedIndividual at lines 127728-127732. The temporal.owl#lantus individual is typed as FTDM.owl#glargine and linked to adverse events, not temporal built-in content, at lines 127216-127223.
findings.explanation: FASTO creates patient, device, drug, adverse-event, and time-unit individuals under namespaces controlled by SSN and the SWRL temporal built-ins ontology. This conflates local FASTO content with external vocabulary ownership, creates IRI collision risk, and makes dependency/provenance management difficult.
findings.suggested_fix: Move FASTO-created individuals to a FASTO- or project-owned namespace. Keep external namespace IRIs only for terms actually owned by those external vocabularies, and add explicit mappings or annotations when a local term corresponds to an external code or standard term.
findings.additional_comment: This finding is not the same as missing labels, missing domains/ranges, or OOPS duplicate/equivalence findings; it concerns namespace ownership of locally minted individuals.

findings.flaw_category: Fragmented namespace policy for conceptually related entities
findings.evidence: FASTO_RDF(6).owl declares both xmlns:FTDM="https://bioportal.bioontology.org/ontologies/FTDM.owl#" and xmlns:FTDM2="https://bioportal.bioontology.org/ontologies/FTDM/" at lines 13 and 23. The class FTDM.owl#aspart is declared at lines 123792-123795, while the individual FTDM/aspart is declared and typed as FTDM.owl#aspart at lines 129413-129421. The same pattern appears for other insulin entities, e.g. FTDM.owl#detemir at lines 124372-124376 and FTDM/detemir is used as an object value at lines 94711-94714. Two FASTOOntologyProperty roots also exist: http://www.w3.org/ns/ssn/FASTOOntologyProperty is a datatype-property superproperty in FASTO_RDF lines 8545-8555, while https://bioportal.bioontology.org/ontologies/FTDM.owl#FASTOOntologyProperty is used as an object-property superproperty at lines 6091-6103.
findings.explanation: The ontology uses multiple IRI bases for closely related FTDM/FASTO modeling constructs, including class/individual pairs with the same local names and separate top properties with the same local name. This makes identity, querying, imports, and refactoring fragile because local-name matching no longer reliably identifies one resource family or modeling layer.
findings.suggested_fix: Define a canonical namespace policy for classes, properties, and individuals. Use stable, distinct IRIs for classes versus instances, and document any intentional class-instance pairing with labels, definitions, and mapping annotations rather than relying on namespace variation alone.
findings.additional_comment: This aggregates the namespace-fragmentation problem; it is not a duplicate-label finding.

findings.flaw_category: Class/individual punning with the same IRI
findings.evidence: FASTO_RDF(6).owl declares https://bioportal.bioontology.org/ontologies/FTDM.owl#pramlintide as an owl:Class at lines 126143-126146 and also declares the exact same IRI as an owl:NamedIndividual at lines 129267-129269. The same IRI is also used as the object of FTDM:drugContradictWithDrug at line 129157.
findings.explanation: The same IRI denotes both the pramlintide class and an individual. OWL 2 punning can be syntactically legal, but it gives the class and individual separate semantic interpretations while sharing one identifier, which is error-prone for maintainers and tools that expect a clean class/instance separation.
findings.suggested_fix: Separate the drug class and any concrete drug/product individual into distinct, clearly named IRIs. Preserve their relationship with a textual annotation or an explicit modeling relation rather than reusing the same IRI for both levels.
findings.additional_comment: This finding is narrower than the self-instantiation baseline reports: the pramlintide individual declaration is not merely an rdf:type self-loop; it is same-IRI class/individual punning.

findings.evidence: FASTO_RDF(6).owl contains misspelled or unstable semantic names: exerciseContradicteWithDrug at lines 7089-7092; diseaseContradictWithDrug has inverse FTDM.owl#drugContradictDithDisease at lines 7664-7668, and that property is declared at lines 7715-7717; hasPreferedBGUoM at lines 8987-8990; hasPreferedInsulinRegimen at lines 10437-10441; isPragnant at lines 10513-10518; ssn/depolyedOnPlatform at lines 6696-6702; ssn/bodyTemprature and bodyTempratureObservation at lines 107077-107090; ssn/measurmentCapability and hasMeasurmentProperty at lines 107493-107502 and 6802-6806; patient_1_exercisePlan_1_part_1_rage_low and related individuals at lines 128981-129003; patient_1_carePlan_1_1ac_goal_status at lines 130091-130108.
findings.explanation: These spelling errors are embedded in IRIs that are used in axioms and assertions, not only in human-readable comments. Such IRIs are hard to discover, easy to duplicate with corrected spellings later, and can lead to inconsistent query and rule logic.
findings.suggested_fix: Create a controlled naming review for ontology IRIs. Deprecate misspelled IRIs, add clear labels/comments during transition, and mint corrected replacement IRIs with explicit migration guidance rather than silently changing existing identifiers.
findings.additional_comment: This finding targets concrete misspellings, not general naming-style variation.

findings.flaw_category: Patient-specific ABox data embedded in the ontology artifact
findings.evidence: FASTO_RDF(6).owl identifies the artifact as an ontology for FASTO at lines 33-40, but the same file declares patient-specific individuals and clinical records. Examples include ssn/patient_1_BAN at lines 127728-127732, FASTO/patient_1 and its personal/clinical assertions at lines 128852-128878, FTDM/patient_1_carePlan_1 with many CarePlan assertions at lines 130066-130088, and FTDM/practitioner_1 at lines 130475-130478.
findings.explanation: Reusable class/property schema and concrete patient/care-plan instance data are co-located in one ontology file. This can make ontology versioning, publication, privacy review, testing, and reuse harder because example or operational ABox data changes at a different cadence from the ontology TBox.
findings.suggested_fix: Separate the reusable ontology schema from example, test, or operational patient instance graphs. Keep links between them through imports or dataset metadata only when the intended deployment requires the example data to be distributed with the ontology.
findings.additional_comment: This is reported as a maintainability risk because the file itself does not state whether the patient records are examples, test fixtures, or intended production ABox content.

findings.flaw_category: External dependency content without explicit owl:imports
findings.evidence: FASTO_RDF(6).owl declares namespaces for DDO, SSN, FTDM, FHIR, OBO, OntoFood-related resources, SWRL, and other external vocabularies at lines 4-31. The ontology metadata says FASTO is based on BFO, SSN, and HL7 FHIR at lines 36-38. The owl:Ontology block at lines 33-43 contains version and annotation metadata but no owl:imports statement; parsing FASTO_RDF(6).owl yields zero owl:imports triples.
findings.explanation: The ontology uses and declares many external terms but does not declare import dependencies in the authoritative RDF/XML artifact. This makes it difficult to determine which external ontology versions are intended, whether the file is a merged release, and how consumers should reconstruct the dependency closure.
findings.suggested_fix: Declare explicit imports for intended external dependencies, or document the artifact as a merged/distribution file with source ontology versions and generation process. Keep dependency metadata in the ontology record so consumers can reproduce the modeling context.
findings.additional_comment: This finding is based on the primary RDF/XML structure and the observed absence of owl:imports, not on OWL profile conformance messages.

findings.flaw_category: Ontology IRI, xml:base, and default namespace mismatch
findings.evidence: FASTO_RDF(6).owl sets the default namespace and xml:base to http://www.semanticweb.org/shaker/ontologies/2018/9/untitled-ontology-475 at lines 1-3, while the ontology IRI is https://bioportal.bioontology.org/ontologies/FASTO.owl at line 33 and the FASTO term namespace is https://bioportal.bioontology.org/ontologies/FASTO/ at line 22.
findings.explanation: The artifact retains a generated or obsolete base IRI that does not match the published ontology IRI or the main FASTO term namespace. If relative IRIs are introduced later, they may resolve into the wrong namespace, and the mismatch also makes the serialization harder to audit.
findings.suggested_fix: Align xml:base and the default namespace with the intended ontology IRI or remove reliance on a generated base. Document the canonical term namespace separately from the ontology document IRI.
findings.additional_comment: No current relative-IRI failure is asserted; the issue is maintainability and future serialization risk.

findings.flaw_category: Fragile special character in IRI local name
findings.evidence: FASTO_RDF(6).owl declares the class IRI with an escaped apostrophe in the RDF/XML attribute: https://bioportal.bioontology.org/ontologies/FASTO/acute_Chagas'_disease at lines 108984-108987. RDF parsing resolves this to https://bioportal.bioontology.org/ontologies/FASTO/acute_Chagas'_disease.
findings.explanation: The apostrophe is part of the identifier, not just the display label. Although parseable in RDF/XML, such punctuation in ontology IRIs can be fragile across Turtle/SPARQL serialization, URL handling, shell tooling, and manual curation.
findings.suggested_fix: Mint a normalized, punctuation-stable IRI and preserve the apostrophe in rdfs:label or synonym annotations. If the existing IRI is published, deprecate it and document the replacement rather than silently rewriting it.
findings.additional_comment: This is a maintainability risk, not a claim that the RDF/XML is syntactically invalid.

findings.flaw_category: FHIR primitive value nodes without literal values
findings.evidence: FASTO_RDF(6).owl uses FHIR primitive wrapper individuals that are referenced as values but lack fhir:hasValue literals. For example, carePlan_1_a1c_goal is typed as http://hl7.org/fhir/decimal with no fhir:hasValue at lines 129452-129456, and is referenced by fhir:Quantity.value at line 129486. carePlan_1_bedTime_target_range_high_decimal is typed decimal with no fhir:hasValue at lines 129530-129534 and is referenced as fhir:Quantity.value at line 129525. patient_1_carePlan_1_fixed_regimen_1_evening_long_quantity_value is typed decimal with no fhir:hasValue at lines 130253-130257 and is referenced as fhir:Quantity.value at line 130248. patient_1_carePlan_1_period_end is typed dateTime with no fhir:hasValue at lines 130376-130380 and is referenced by fhir:Period.end at line 130370.
findings.explanation: Several individuals function as FHIR primitive value containers but do not carry the literal value that the surrounding quantity or period structure points to. This can leave care-plan targets, regimen quantities, exercise-plan quantities, or period endpoints semantically incomplete unless another rule or data source fills them later.
findings.suggested_fix: For each primitive wrapper that is intended to carry a value, add the literal value in the source data graph. If a value is intentionally unknown or to be inferred later, annotate or model that status explicitly and avoid asserting a concrete value node that contains no value.
findings.additional_comment: The finding does not rely on datatype correctness judgments from the verbalizer. It is based on RDF/XML assertions and missing fhir:hasValue triples for referenced primitive nodes.
